intro.heading: Restore Jaw Health with Bone Grafting in Santa Clarita
paragraphs: Bone grafting may sound intimidating, but at Valencia Dentistry, it’s a carefully planned and comfortable procedure designed to rebuild lost bone and provide a stable foundation for your smile. Whether you’re preparing for dental implants, recovering from tooth loss, or restoring facial contours, our bone grafting treatments in Santa Clarita are performed using advanced digital technology and a personalized, compassionate approach. Dr. Lavi and our experienced team are here to make sure your experience is stress-free—from your first consultation to full recovery.

understanding.heading: Types of Bone Grafting Materials We Use
understanding.intro: For patients seeking all-natural, biocompatible treatment options, we offer regenerative techniques that align with holistic values and avoid synthetic materials. These options harness the body’s own healing power for safer, more natural outcomes:

image.alt: Bone Grafting: treatment at Valencia Dentistry

items.title: Allograft
items.text: Sourced from donated human bone, this type is thoroughly processed and contains no living cells. What remains is a mineral matrix with natural growth factors (chemoreceptors) that signal your body to rebuild bone in the treated area.

items.title: Xenograft
items.text: Made from animal bone (often bovine), xenografts are also processed to remove all organic material, leaving behind a strong bone scaffold.

items.title: Synthetic Graft
items.text: Lab-made materials designed to mimic natural bone structure, often used when patients prefer non-biological sources.

items.title: PRF (Platelet-Rich Fibrin)
items.text: Made from your own blood to promote faster healing, reduce inflammation, and support tissue regeneration.

items.title: Autologous Bone Grafting
items.text: Uses bone from another area of your mouth—no foreign materials involved.

items.title: No Synthetic Additives
items.text: A fully organic approach ideal for those prioritizing natural healing and wellness.

process.heading: What Is a Bone Grafting Procedure?
process.intro: Bone grafting is a specialized procedure that restores or builds up bone in the jaw—often needed after tooth loss, trauma, or infection. At our Valencia, CA practice, this treatment is commonly used to prepare the jaw for dental implants or to prevent long-term bone deterioration after an extraction. Without enough healthy bone, placing dental implants or maintaining proper facial structure becomes difficult. That’s where bone grafting comes in—it rebuilds the foundation of your smile.

steps.title: Socket Preservation
steps.text: Placed immediately after a tooth is removed, this graft maintains bone height and width for future implant placement.

steps.title: Ridge Augmentation
steps.text: Restores the natural contour of the jawbone, especially after trauma or prolonged tooth loss, to provide a stable foundation for implants.

steps.title: Sinus Lift
steps.text: Adds bone to the upper jaw below the sinus area, commonly done when placing implants in the back upper teeth.

steps.title: Consultation & Imaging
steps.text: Your journey begins with a detailed exam and 3D digital scan to assess your bone volume and determine the best grafting approach. Dr. Lavi will explain your options and answer any questions, so you feel fully informed and supported.

steps.title: In-Office Bone Graft Procedure
steps.text: The grafting procedure is performed right here in our Valencia, CA office using local anesthesia and optional sedation. We place the bone graft material in the targeted area, then protect and stabilize the site to begin the healing process.

steps.title: Healing & Follow-Up
steps.text: Depending on your case, healing can take several weeks to a few months. We’ll schedule follow-up visits to monitor your progress and let you know when your jaw is ready for the next step—such as dental implant placement.

candidate.heading: Who Is a Good Candidate for Bone Grafting?
candidate.text: Bone grafting is often recommended for patients who have experienced jawbone loss or need to build up bone before receiving dental implants. You may be a strong candidate if you: During your consultation, Dr. Lavi will assess your oral health, take detailed 3D scans, and determine whether bone grafting is right for you.
bullets: Lost a tooth and want to preserve jawbone structure
Plan to get dental implants but lack sufficient bone density
Have experienced facial sagging or bone deterioration due to missing teeth
Need to restore stability and function to your bite

care.heading: Pre- and Post-Op Instructions for Bone Grafting
care.intro: Your comfort and healing are our top priorities. That’s why we provide clear, personalized guidance to help you prepare for your bone graft—and recover smoothly afterward. Here’s what to expect before and after your procedure: Before Your Procedure: How to Prepare After Your Procedure: How to Heal
before: Follow any fasting instructions if sedation is planned
Avoid smoking or alcohol for at least 24 hours before your appointment
Pause medications only if advised by Dr. Lavi
Arrange for transportation home if sedation is used
Keep up with good oral hygiene to reduce the risk of infection
Rest for the first 24–48 hours and avoid strenuous activity
after: Use cold compresses to manage swelling
Take all prescribed medications as directed
Eat soft, cool foods like yogurt, smoothies, and applesauce
Avoid straws, smoking, or forceful rinsing
Rinse gently with saltwater to keep the area clean

faqs.a: Most patients report minimal discomfort. We use local anesthesia and offer sedation options to keep you relaxed throughout the procedure. Mild soreness afterward is common and easily managed with medication.

faqs.q: How long does it take to heal after a bone graft?
faqs.a: Initial healing typically takes a few weeks, but full bone integration can take 3–6 months depending on your health and the type of graft. We’ll monitor your progress with regular follow-ups.

faqs.q: Can I get a dental implant immediately after bone grafting?
faqs.a: In some cases, yes—but most patients need to wait for the grafted bone to heal and fully integrate before implant placement. Dr. Lavi will create a timeline that fits your needs.

faqs.q: What kind of bone is used for grafting?
faqs.a: We use safe, biocompatible materials sourced from your own body, a donor, or synthetic alternatives—depending on your condition and preference. Each option is carefully explained during your consultation.
